found.description: Chronic alcohol use (3+ drinks/day) combined with acetaminophen significantly increases risk of hepatotoxicity. FDA requires alcohol warning on all acetaminophen OTC labels.
found.management: Avoid acetaminophen or limit to <2g/day if drinking regularly.

sources.name: FDA OTC monograph / clinical literature: acetaminophen + ethanol

found.description: Ibuprofen can interfere with aspirin's antiplatelet effect when taken within 30 minutes before or 8 hours after aspirin. Both increase GI bleeding risk.
found.management: Take aspirin at least 30 min before ibuprofen. Consider alternatives.

sources.name: FDA OTC monograph / clinical literature: ibuprofen + aspirin

found.description: Two NSAIDs taken together do not provide additional pain relief but significantly increase risk of GI ulcers, bleeding, and kidney damage.
found.management: Never combine two NSAIDs. Use one or the other.

sources.name: FDA OTC monograph / clinical literature: ibuprofen + naproxen sodium

found.description: Diphenhydramine (found in Benadryl, NyQuil, ZzzQuil, many sleep aids) combined with alcohol causes additive CNS depression: extreme drowsiness, impaired coordination, risk of respiratory depression.
found.management: Avoid alcohol entirely when taking diphenhydramine.

sources.name: FDA OTC monograph / clinical literature: diphenhydramine + ethanol

full_pool.description: Bismuth subsalicylate (Pepto-Bismol) contains salicylate. Combined with aspirin, total salicylate load can cause toxicity, especially in children (Reye's syndrome risk).
full_pool.management: Avoid combining. Do not give either to children with viral illness.
